title: How to Get Painting Leads
html:
Start with the free sources, add Google Ads on repaint searches, and buy leads only when the price is below what your close rate allows.

What you need first

You need five things before you chase painting leads. They are a business profile, a phone that gets answered, a simple website, photos of finished jobs and a way to track each call. Without these, new leads leak out.

Which painting lead sources work best?

Google Ads and bought leads bring calls fastest, referrals and Meta ads follow, and your profile, reviews and SEO build slowly but cost the least. Pick two or three to start instead of trying all of them.

The table sorts sources by how soon they usually bring a first call.

Painting lead sources by typical speed to first call, 2026. Speed varies by market.

Steps to get painting leads

These 8 steps run from free to paid. Do steps 1 and 2 first, add the rest as your schedule and budget allow.

1. Complete your Google Business Profile

Fill out every field of your profile so you show up in local map searches. The profile is free and it is the first thing many homeowners see.

  • Choose painter as the main category and add interior and exterior painting services.
  • Upload real photos of finished jobs and your crew.
  • Set your service area to the cities you actually serve.

Checkpoint: the profile shows your correct phone, hours and at least 10 photos.

Mistake to avoid: using a stock photo of a roller instead of your own work.

2. Ask for a review after every job

Send a review link the day you finish a paint job. Reviews are what a homeowner compares first when two painters look alike.

  • Text the direct review link before the crew leaves.
  • Reply to each review within a week.
  • Add the new review count to your tracking sheet.

Mistake to avoid: waiting for a quiet month to ask, since people forget.

3. Build a page for each job type

Give interior, exterior, cabinet and commercial painting their own pages. One page per job type lets you show up for each search.

  • Write 300 words per page with your process and a price range you can honor.
  • Add three photos and a short customer quote.
  • Put your phone number and a quote form above the fold.

Mistake to avoid: one page that lists every service in a single paragraph.

4. Run Google Ads on repaint searches

Bid on searches that show intent, such as painters near me and exterior house painting. Paid search puts you above the map on the day a homeowner is ready.

  • Start with a daily budget you can afford for 30 days.
  • Target your real service area and add negative keywords like jobs and diy.
  • Send each ad to the matching job-type page.

See Google Ads for painters or PPC management for painting companies .

5. Use Meta ads for exterior season

Run Facebook and Instagram ads with before and after photos when exterior repaint season starts. Meta shows your work to homeowners who were not searching yet.

  • Use a before and after photo set from one finished house.
  • Target homeowners within your service area.
  • Send them to a short quote form.

Checkpoint: cost per lead stays within your target after two weeks. Meta ads management is $1,999 a month plus ad spend; see Meta ads for painters.

Mistake to avoid: running the ads year round when demand dips in winter.

Get the free contractor marketing guide

Meet realtors, property managers and general contractors who need a reliable painter. One partner can send repeat jobs for years.

  • Offer a quick turnaround to realtors who list homes.
  • Leave a short info sheet with property managers.
  • Place a yard sign at every job with the owner's permission.

Checkpoint: log every partner lead in your tracking sheet. Mistake to avoid: handing out flyers with no way to track which one worked.

Buy a lead only when its price is below what your close rate allows. Shared leads go to several painters at once, so you race to call first.

Use this rule: maximum lead price equals your close rate times your gross profit per job, then halve it to leave profit.

Sample math with made-up numbers: if a shared lead closes at 20% and a job leaves $800 in gross profit, the cap is $80. If an exclusive lead closes at 40%, the cap is $160. Use your own close rate.

Checkpoint: compare cost per booked job from lead vendors with your Google Ads cost per booked job every month. Mistake to avoid: buying a contract that locks in lead volume you cannot close.

8. Answer fast, quote fast and track every lead

Call back every lead the same day and send a written quote within two days. Speed beats price for many homeowners, and it costs nothing.

  • Send the first text within minutes of a form.
  • Book an on-site estimate before you hang up.
  • Log the quote and the result in your tracking sheet.

Checkpoint: every lead has a status. Mistake to avoid: sending a quote with no follow-up call.

How do you know your painting lead plan is working?

Your plan is working when five numbers hold steady: cost per lead, close rate, return on ad spend, answered calls and new reviews. Check them monthly, and change one thing at a time.

Common painting lead problems and fixes

Most painting lead problems come from three causes: leads outside your area, slow follow-up and poor tracking. The fixes are simple and cost almost nothing.

Pay for a lead only when your close rate says it can pay you back.

How much do painting leads cost?

Painting lead cost depends on your market, the job type and whether the lead is shared or exclusive. Calculate your own cap by multiplying close rate by gross profit per job, then halve it.

Are painting lead companies worth it?

Painting lead companies can fill gaps in your schedule, but they give you little control and often sell a lead to several painters. Compare the cost per booked job with your own Google Ads results each month. If you run Performance Max, read the latest Performance Max brand query update before you compare results. Keep the vendor only if it books jobs below your cost cap.

What is a good cost per lead for painters?

A good number for you is one that stays below your cap: close rate times gross profit per job, halved. A cheap lead that never books is more expensive than a costly one that does.

Final advice

Start with your profile and reviews this week, then add Google Ads when you can answer every call. If you want help, a home services marketing agency can set up the tracking, ads and reviews. That way the leads you pay for turn into booked jobs.
